conventions.convention: Countable Choice is assumed throughout the scattering contract and inherited by its consumers.
Translations use p·a = p⁰a⁰ − p⃗·a⃗ and positive-energy joint PVM support. The shell parameter m > 0 has inverse-length units and is not identified with a measured rest mass.
The packet Fourier integral has prefactor (2π)⁻³ and phase i k·x − iηℓ₀tωₘ(k). The dimensionless parameter satisfies t ≥ 1; η = +1 means outgoing and η = −1 means incoming.
Fock sectors retain the supplier's second-variable-linear pairing; the Cook theorem explicitly uses its first-variable-linear counterpart (f,g)F,1 = ⟨g,f⟩F,2.

The completed asymptotic space is the closure of the packet domain, without an assertion that this closure equals the whole Fock space. Unitary means surjective isometry; full asymptotic completeness additionally requires both scattering ranges to equal the target Hilbert space.

load_bearing.statement: This is a contract for a proof, not an existence theorem. It does not derive the Cook bound, the one-particle limits, or the Fock inner-product limits from locality and shell isolation.

For each η,f, the stated norm-C¹ derivative bound Cη,f(1+t)⁻¹⁻εη,f with Cη,f ≥ 0 and εη,f > 0 yields a norm limit Wηf and error at most (Cη,f/εη,f)(1+t)⁻εη,f. Linearity and convergence of pairwise inner products to the specified Fock pairing additionally yield an isometry extending uniquely to the packet-domain closure.

For the two isometric Cook extensions Ω± from the completed packet space to H, S = Ω+*Ω− is a contraction. It is unitary if and only if Ran Ω+ = Ran Ω−. Full asymptotic completeness is the stronger condition Ran Ω+ = Ran Ω− = H.

published_dependencies.used_for: The explicit choice premise inherited by the integration, Fourier, tensor-completion and adjoint interfaces.
The precise unital complex star-algebra operations used for the bounded operator algebra.
Future-shell coordinates, inverse-length shell parameter, and the explicitly signed Fourier pairing.
Completed symmetric and antisymmetric tensor sectors, vacuum sector, Fock direct sum and second-variable-linear pairing.
Strong measurability via pointwise norm limits of measurable simple functions.
The definition of the vector integral through integrable simple approximations.
Existence of each smeared vector integral from strong measurability and integrability of its norm.
The smeared-operator norm bound and the Cook increment estimate.
Finite scalar PVM measures, complex matrix-coefficient measures and the first-variable-linear polarization formula.
Bounded packet multipliers and their matrix-coefficient integral representation.
Continuity, hence Borel measurability, of the scalar spectral multiplier obtained by spatial integration.
Interchanging spatial Lebesgue integration and integration against finite positive scalar PVM measures after polarization.
The rescaled Fourier identity giving the exact mass-shell component of the smeared vacuum vector.
Expressing Cook increments as Bochner integrals of the continuous norm derivative on compact intervals.
The unit-ball characterization of vector norm and the contraction estimate for an isometry's adjoint.
Existence and boundedness of adjoints and reversal of compositions in the scattering-range criterion.
